document.title: Deck Apps ship their own host plugin as a .vdplugin package
document.summary: Host Control Plugins move to two kinds: built-ins (`core`, `systemStats`) inside the Host Companion, and a Deck App's own plugin, which `vitadeck build` turns from `hostPlugin` into a `<slug>.vdplugin` package folder and `.vdplugin.zip` that `vitadeck-host-companion install` unpacks and hot-reloads.
document.why: Máté asked that [authors keep the plugin and the Deck App in one repo, without an npm package](source:s1), that [built-in plugins cover the use cases with custom ones only when needed](source:s1), that plugin loading get simpler, and that [the global CLI be called vitadeck-host-companion](source:s1).

sources.label: Claude Code session · Oct 29
sources.gist: Máté asks for same-repo plugins, built-ins, easier loading (maybe a .vdplugin), a vitadeck-host-companion bin, and a look at a single vitadeck CLI, then a compromise.

sources.label: PR #145
sources.title: feat(host-control): Deck Apps ship their own host plugin as one .vdplugin file
sources.gist: Built-ins first, a .vdplugin per Deck App, install/remove and hot reload, two CLIs; stacked on #144.

sources.label: chatgpt-codex-connector on PR #145
sources.author: chatgpt-codex-connector
sources.body: Derive the plugin path from the configured app name. If an author changes vitadeck.config.json's name so its slug differs from the scaffold's original project slug, vitadeck build writes the plugin under the new slug, but this host script still passes the original filename.

lookFor: Done as asked later in [the session](source:s1): a `.vdplugin` is a vdapp-like package (`manifest.json`, bundled `companion.mjs`, optional `files/`) with a `.vdplugin.zip` whose one top-level entry is that folder; the first commits shipped a single JS file and the format changed in a601a6ca.

Considered, not chosen: [the request](source:s1) floated a single `vitadeck` CLI. The companion keeps its own bin, `vitadeck-host-companion`, because a second bin in `@vitadeck/sdk` breaks `npx @vitadeck/sdk` and users would install Babel and rolldown to run a server.

Not true at head: `@vitadeck/host-companion` is still `private: true`, so a project from `create --host-plugin` cannot `npm install` its `@vitadeck/host-companion` devDependency until the package is published; [PR #145](source:s2) tests with packed tarballs instead.

groups.title: SDK: plugin implementation API and the systemStats registry
groups.why: Authors write both halves of a plugin against `@vitadeck/sdk/host-control` alone, so a plugin needs no companion package; the other groups build on these exports.
groups.summary: `implementHostPlugin`, `HostCommandError`, `ImplementedHostPlugin` and the `HostPluginManifest` contract move into the SDK's `plugin.ts`, and the `systemStatsPlugin` registry moves from `js/host-plugins` into `system-stats.ts`, all re-exported from `index.ts`.
lookFor: `implementHostPlugin` now ships inside every Deck App bundle that imports `@vitadeck/sdk/host-control`, though rolldown tree-shakes it from apps that never call it.

groups.title: Companion: built-ins and loading Host Plugin Packages
groups.why: A globally installed companion has to load a plugin from a package folder rather than a package name, the package has to carry files besides code, and a rebuilt package has to replace the running one.
groups.summary: `loadHostPluginPackage` reads a `.vdplugin` folder's manifest and imports its entry by file URL with a content-hash query, `extractHostPluginArchive` unpacks a `.vdplugin.zip`, and the server's new `setPlugins` swaps every plugin but `core`, while `systemStats` becomes a built-in implementation beside `core`.
lookFor: Subtle: `HostCommandError` is matched by `name` and a wire `code`, not `instanceof`, because each package bundles its own copy of the class; any thrown `Error` named `HostCommandError` with a wire code now maps to that code.

The entry is imported as `<file URL>?v=<sha256 of the entry>`, so a rebuilt entry loads fresh, but a rebuild that changes only `files/` keeps the cached module; a plugin must read `files/` when a command runs.

`extractHostPluginArchive` rejects archives with more than one top-level folder (after dropping `__MACOSX/`), backslashes, empty segments and `..`, and writes no file modes, so a shipped script loses its exec bit.
Plugin ids must match `/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,126}$/` at load; an id like `../x` is rejected because `install` names the folder after it.

groups.title: Companion CLI: vitadeck-host-companion install, remove and hot reload
groups.why: This is the user's side of [simpler plugin loading](source:s1) and the [vitadeck-host-companion name](source:s1).
groups.summary: `start` loads the built-ins, every package in `~/.vitadeck/plugins/` and each `--plugin` package or folder of packages, watches those folders recursively and calls `setPlugins` after changes, while `install` stages an archive or folder in `.install-*`, validates it and renames it to `<id>.vdplugin`, and `remove` deletes that folder.
lookFor: Paths resolve against `INIT_CWD` only when `npm_lifecycle_event` is `host-companion` (the repo's own script); a Deck App's `host` script and a global install resolve against the working directory.

A `--plugin` package wins over an installed plugin with the same id, so an author can run a build of a plugin they also installed; a reload that throws logs `Kept the previous plugins` and keeps serving the old set.

`--plugin` decides by name: a path ending in `.vdplugin` is one package, a `.vdplugin.zip` is refused with a pointer to `install`, and anything else is a folder of packages, which is how the scaffold's `--plugin ./dist` picks up a renamed app, answering [Codex's review](source:s3).
An existing config with the old `plugins` field still loads; `readConfig` ignores the field, and `systemStats` is loaded as a built-in anyway.

groups.title: SDK CLI: build writes the .vdplugin package and zip, create --host-plugin scaffolds it
groups.why: Authors [keep the plugin and the Deck App in one repo, with scaffold help](source:s1).
groups.summary: `hostPlugin: { entry, files? }` in `vitadeck.config.json` makes `build` bundle the entry with rolldown into a staged `<slug>.vdplugin` folder with `manifest.json` and a copied `files/`, swap it into `outDir` and zip it like the `.vdapp`, while `create --host-plugin` lays the `templates/host-plugin` overlay over the scaffold, merging its JSON files one level deep.
lookFor: A failed plugin build leaves the previous `<slug>.vdplugin` in place: the package is written to `<slug>.vdplugin.tmp` and renamed over the old folder only after the bundle, `files/` copy and manifest succeed.
`hostPlugin.files` must be a folder inside the project other than its root; links in it are copied as the files they point to, so the folder and the zip hold the same files.

The `.vdplugin.zip` is written beside the `.vdapp.zip`; `vitadeck dev` rebuilds the package every cycle but only uploads the `.vdapp.zip`, and the scaffold's `host` script runs the companion with `--plugin ./dist`.

The new root devDependency `@vitadeck/sdk` in `js/package.json` exists so the overlay template, which sits outside any workspace package, resolves `@vitadeck/sdk` for the SDK's `tsc` and type-aware lint.

groups.title: Companion package, workspace and the demo app
groups.why: The companion becomes something users install globally, and the old `js/host-plugins` package has nowhere left to live.
groups.summary: The companion's `package.json` gains the `vitadeck-host-companion` bin and a rolldown build that inlines the SDK so it has no dependencies, `js/host-plugins` leaves the workspace, and the demo Deck App and Shell hint switch to the built-in registry and the new command name.
lookFor: The demo's `failureHint` loses its `unknown_plugin` branch, since `systemStats` is now always present on a current companion.
The root `build` script now also builds the companion, so the host CMake build's JS step runs it too.

groups.title: Docs: ADR 0004, glossary and READMEs
groups.why: AGENTS.md asks that a change fix the ADR, CONTEXT.md and READMEs it makes inaccurate, in place.
groups.summary: ADR 0004's plugin section is rewritten for built-ins, Host Plugin Files and the two CLIs, CONTEXT.md adds **Host Plugin File**, and the companion, SDK and demo READMEs switch to the published install and the `--host-plugin` workflow.

commits.subject: fix(sdk): build the plugin package beside the old one and swap it in
commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: fix(host-control): a broken plugin build keeps the last good package
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Bundle before replacing the package folder, copy linked files as files, and
require hostPlugin.files to be a folder. The companion ignores __MACOSX/ in
archives and points a --plugin .zip at install. Docs say the zip keeps no
file modes and that files/ is read per call.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(host-control): a Deck App's plugin ships as a .vdplugin package and zip
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Plugins will carry more than code (scripts, data, binaries), so the single
bundled file becomes a package like the Deck App's: `vitadeck build` writes a
<slug>.vdplugin folder (manifest.json, companion.mjs, optional files/) and a
<slug>.vdplugin.zip. `hostPlugin` becomes { entry, files? }. The companion
installs archives or folders into ~/.vitadeck/plugins/<id>.vdplugin, loads the
entry by file URL so it finds its files through import.meta.url, and watches
package folders recursively.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(host-companion): --plugin takes a directory, so the scaffold survives a renamed app
commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: fix(host-companion): allow plugin ids as long as a package slug
commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: fix(host-companion): rename the plugin's module copy into place
commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: fix(host-companion): install renames the plugin into place
commits.author: Máté Molnár

commits.subject: fix(host-companion): load plugins from file copies, resolve paths from the cwd
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A bundled CommonJS dependency calls createRequire(import.meta.url), which a
data: URL cannot satisfy; plugins now load from a content-hashed .mjs copy.
Paths resolve against the working directory except under the repo's own
`host-companion` script, so a Deck App's `host` script works from anywhere.
Plugin ids may start with a digit, and watcher errors are logged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(host-control): built-in plugins, .vdplugin files, vitadeck-host-companion
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A Deck App now keeps its own Host Control Plugin in its project: `hostPlugin`
in vitadeck.config.json makes `vitadeck build` bundle the implementation into
one self-contained <slug>.vdplugin, and `vitadeck create --host-plugin`
scaffolds it. Users install that file with `vitadeck-host-companion install`;
the companion reloads installed and --plugin files when they change.

systemStats moves into the companion as a built-in, with its registry in
@vitadeck/sdk/host-control next to implementHostPlugin and HostCommandError.
The companion is a dependency-free bundled package with the
vitadeck-host-companion bin, and js/host-plugins is gone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
